name: Steele-Reese Foundation Idaho and Montana Grant Program (Rural Conservation)
summary: Foundation grants for locally focused land, water and wildlife conservation and ecosystem protection in rural Idaho and Montana and Native nations there, applied for through a letter of inquiry.

steps: Call the Western Director first, if requesting $40,000+ for one year

eligibility.rule: Be a federally tax-exempt entity, not an individual
Benefit rural communities in Idaho, Montana or Native nations sharing this geography
Avoid urban, suburban and nearby urbanized areas
Not endowments, emergencies, charity drives, conferences, documentaries, research, camps, elections or promoting beliefs
LOI submitted by a paid employee, or a board member if there are no paid staff

status.quote: We received 100 LOIs before January 18, 2026, closed the process on that date

opens.quote: We will open the LOI process on January 12, 2026.

geography.quote: makes grants only to federally tax-exempt entities for work in rural Idaho and Montana communities

access.quote: the application process begins with a Letter of Inquiry (LOI) that must be submitted via the Foundation's online grant portal.

window.quote: We will open the LOI process on January 12, 2026. We will close it once we have received 100 LOIs, which may be within days.

applicant_types.quote: The Steele-Reese Foundation makes grants only to federally tax-exempt entities

effort.quote: If you are requesting a grant of $40,000 or more for a single year, before submitting a letter of inquiry you must first have a conversation specifically about the amount of your request with Western Director Linda Tracy at 406/207-7984.
the application process begins with a Letter of Inquiry (LOI) that must be submitted via the Foundation’s online grant portal.

By March 2, 2026, we will respond to all organizations that submit an LOI to either invite them to complete full applications by April 1, 2026, or to let them know that we are unable to further consider their proposals.

eligibility.quote: No grants are made to individuals or to entities that have not been recognized as federally tax-exempt by the Internal Revenue Service.
The Foundation will only consider requests that benefit rural communities in Idaho, Montana, and in Native nations with whom we share this geography.
We will not consider requests for work benefiting urban or suburban areas, or those more rural areas immediately adjacent, or in close proximity, to an urbanized area.

Endowment funds Emergencies Community funds and charity drives Conferences and workshops or their related travel Documentaries Efforts to influence elections directly or indirectly Planning, research, or experimental projects Athletic or academic competitions, or related travel Summer camps Efforts to promulgate religious or political beliefs or agendas
However, the person submitting an LOI must be an employee of the organization requesting funds or if there is no paid staff, a member of its Board of Directors.

after_award.quote: In the interest of transparency about the grant process, this packet also includes a list of application questions we will ask of those we later invite to submit full applications, and the final report questions we will ask in the summer of 2027 of those who receive grants.
